item: tests: every item (N) that RULINGS_INDEX.md cites resolves to exactly one OPEN_QUEUE.md entry
summary: Measured first: OPEN_QUEUE.md has 127 lines opening '(N) **', mostly numbered points inside one prose entry, so the numbering restarts in every numbered list: (1) to (13) appear 4 to 16 times each, (14) to (17) twice, and only (18) to (30) once; RULINGS_INDEX.md has ten citations of the shape 'item (N)' naming six items (20, 21, 26, 28, 29, 30), all of which resolve to exactly one opener. The test therefore pins 'a cited number has exactly one entry' (a missing number and an ambiguous one are both refused) and not contiguity, which would say nothing below 18. Mutants: citing item (99), dropping entry (21) and duplicating entry (28) each turn the resolution test red; renaming the citation phrase turns the reader-liveness test red. Limits stated in the docstring: section-named citations ('OPEN_QUEUE 27 Oct, item 13') and the bare '(item N)' shape are not read (R233's '(item 37)' is a lane bundle item, not a queue entry), so a wrong number in those shapes is invisible; it checks the opener exists, not that the row's claim about it is true.
